<p class="lede">AI agents plan, use tools, and act over time, so a single final answer is a weak test. This tutorial covers why agent evaluation is hard, how LLM-as-a-judge methods work, a hands-on exercise, and the reliability limits of model-based judges.</p>

## What the tutorial covers

From the [ALTA 2026 program](https://alta2026.alta.asn.au/program#afternoon-tutorial):

1. **AI Agents and Evaluation Challenges** — agents, tool use, and why final-answer scoring is not enough.
2. **LLM-as-a-Judge Methods** — criteria, rubrics, scales, prompts, and the trade-offs with rules and human review.
3. **Hands-on Agent Evaluation Exercise** — build a rubric and a judge, then look at tool choice, parameters, and response quality.
4. **Reliability, Limitations, and Future Directions** — consistency, cost, failure modes, and open research.

Presenters: Parvin Zarei Eskikand (SEEK), Terrence Szymanski (SEEK), Sara Mirabi (Deakin University), and Yelaman Abdullin (Macquarie University).

Participants should bring a laptop. Basic familiarity with machine learning, NLP, and large language models is enough. LLM access for the exercise will be confirmed before the tutorial.
